reason: The cited evidence supports that SRO exists and can be enhanced by heat treatment (E3), and that SRO increases dislocation glide resistance and strength (E1, E2). However, none of the cited passages provide evidence for the nucleation of nanoscale precipitates via aging, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Aging heat treatment can induce chemical short-range order (SRO) in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Aging heat treatment can nucleate nanoscale precipitates in these alloys.
SRO and nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
These obstacles increase yield strength and work hardening rate.
The effect is observable in FCC-structured alloys under similar testing conditions.
